official.deadline_note: Published in the MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027: HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01 with a 2026 budget of EUR 628.03 million and deadline 24 November 2026; HORIZON-MSCA-2027-DN-01 with an indicative budget of EUR 645.99 million and deadline 23 November 2027.
official.status_note: The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01) is open with a deadline of 24 November 2026 as published in the Work Programme 2026-2027 and on the DN action page (last updated 29 September 2026).
benefits: Living allowance: EUR 4,250 per person-month (a gross amount including compulsory deductions under national law; a country correction coefficient applies and a top-up may be paid to complement it)
Mobility allowance: EUR 710 per person-month, covering the doctoral candidate's private mobility-related costs (e.g. travel and accommodation costs)
Family allowance: EUR 660 per person-month x % covered by the beneficiary, for researchers with family obligations
Long-term leave allowance and special needs allowance, where applicable (requested unit)
Research, training and networking contribution: EUR 1,600 per person-month; management and indirect contribution: EUR 1,200 per person-month at institutional level
eligibility: Doctoral candidates funded by Doctoral Networks must not have a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment, can be of any nationality and should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project

Mobility rule: doctoral candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date

Doctoral Networks are open to international consortia of universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs and other non-academic organisations, including at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and with at least one of them established in an EU Member State; other organisations from any country in the world can also join
Industrial Doctorate candidates must be enrolled in a doctoral programme, jointly supervised by the academic and non-academic partners, and spend at least 50% of their time outside academia

Joint Doctorate candidates must be enrolled in a joint programme and be jointly supervised, within programmes leading to a joint doctoral degree or multiple doctoral degrees awarded by the participating institutions
requirements: Candidates wishing to apply for PhD positions should apply to funded Doctoral Network projects by consulting their open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal
Consortia apply through the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal; the completed proposal including all annexes is submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call
As from 2022, resubmission restrictions apply for applications that received a score below 80% the previous year
Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate and can also organise secondments for them anywhere in the world
selection_criteria: Impact, excellence and quality of implementation criteria apply as set out in the MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027
As from 2022, resubmission restrictions apply for applications that received a score below 80% the previous year
coverage: Living allowance of EUR 4,250 per person-month (gross; country correction coefficient applies)
Mobility allowance of EUR 710 per person-month for private mobility-related costs including travel and accommodation
Family allowance, long-term leave allowance and special needs allowance where applicable
Research, training and networking costs (EUR 1,600 per person-month) plus management and indirect costs (EUR 1,200 per person-month) covered at institutional level
application_method: Identify an open MSCA Doctoral Networks call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01, deadline 24 November 2026) and its list of funded networks
Consortia find partners and apply through the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, submitting the completed proposal including all annexes by the call deadline
PhD candidates apply to the funded networks' open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal which is updated daily
official.application_route: Watch the DN funding page and the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal for the call; PhD applicants go to EURAXESS to find and apply to the funded networks' advertised vacancies.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - candidates can be of any nationality, and other organisations from any country in the world can join the networks, subject to the mobility rule
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All areas of research may be funded; networks are built across sectors and countries, with Industrial and Joint Doctorates as incentive variants
official.research_requirement: Candidates must not hold a doctoral degree at recruitment and should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project; Industrial Doctorate candidates are jointly supervised and spend at least 50% of their time outside academia, and Joint Doctorate candidates are enrolled in a joint programme under joint supervision
official.duration: Networks last up to 4 years (up to 5 years for Joint Doctorate projects); each fellowship is between 3 and 36 months (between 3 and 48 months for Joint Doctorate fellowships)
official.description: MSCA Doctoral Networks implement doctoral programmes by partnerships of universities, research institutions and socio-economic actors from different countries across Europe and beyond, recruiting doctoral candidates on living and mobility allowances with institutional research, training, networking, management and indirect funding; Industrial Doctorates and Joint Doctorates are incentive variants.
official.region: Europe and beyond (consortia across Europe and beyond)
official.program_type: EU research and innovation mobility action (Doctoral Networks / European Joint Doctorates)

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to MSCA Doctoral Networks yourself - the networks apply, and you compete for the doctoral fellow positions they advertise, so finding an open call and its vacancies is the whole game. Each funded position carries a living allowance of EUR 4,250 a month (gross, before the country correction coefficient), a EUR 710 mobility allowance for your private travel and accommodation costs, and EUR 1,600 per month routed through the host for research and training. The 2026 call closes on 24 November 2026 with EUR 628.03 million behind it, and the 2027 call is already dated for 23 November 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's graduates looking for a funded, internationally supervised PhD position inside a multi-partner European research network.
application_readiness_checklist: Monitor the DN funding page for the HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01 call and its list of funded networks and advertised fellow positions
Check your residence history against the mobility rule: no more than 12 months in the recruiting country during the 36 months before recruitment
Verify you are not yet a doctor at the time of recruitment - awarded PhDs are ineligible
Prepare a research CV and motivation targeted at the network's intersectoral and interdisciplinary training offer, not a generic PhD form
common_rejection_risks: Failing the mobility rule because of a previous stay in the recruiting country
Applying after the doctorate is awarded - doctoral candidates only
Missing the network's own advert deadline inside the call window: recruitment happens per position
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The allowance is gross and subject to tax and social security deductions and the country correction coefficient; no tuition component is published for this action.
document_audit: Requirements are set per network in the position advertisement, so read the specific vacancy rather than the call's general text
alerts: Fellowship length varies: 3-36 months, or 3-48 months if you join a European Joint Doctorate
The 2027 call budget is published as indicative at EUR 645.99 million - scale can shift
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Wait for the network call, track each network's advertised positions, apply directly to the position (network-level recruitment), and the network consortium handles the submission to the European Commission.

official.status_note: The official timeline: applications opened August 2026 and closed October 2026 (country/territory deadlines, 11:00 UTC); the Bangladesh page confirms applications for the 2027-2028 Chevening Scholarships are now closed. Results are expected mid-June 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official scholarships page describes Chevening Scholarships as fully-funded; the award's departure allowance and travel provider are referenced in the official FAQs, while graduation costs are explicitly not covered.
benefits: Chevening Scholarships are fully-funded one-year master's degrees in the UK
The official FAQs reference a departure allowance you can use towards departure-related costs and Chevening's travel provider for flights
The FAQs state Chevening is unable to cover any costs associated with your graduation, including flight tickets to and from the UK for graduation ceremonies
eligibility: To apply you must be a citizen of a Chevening eligible country or territory
You must return to your country of citizenship for a minimum of two years after your award ends
You must have completed at least two years' work experience - 2,800 hours - after completing your undergraduate degree
You must have completed your undergraduate degree at least two years before the application deadline
You must apply to three different eligible UK courses and have received an unconditional offer from one of them
requirements: Upload documents at least seven working days before your interview
Provide evidence of your work experience in hours across the period since your undergraduate degree
Hold an unconditional offer from one of your three chosen UK courses
selection_criteria: Applications are sifted against eligibility criteria (from October 2026)
Reading committee assessments run from mid-October 2026 to January 2027
Interview shortlist issued mid-February 2027; interviews March-April 2027; results mid-June 2027
coverage: Fully-funded one-year master's degree in the UK: university course fees plus support for living costs and travel
application_method: Check the Chevening application timeline for the country/territory deadline in the October window (11:00 UTC)
Apply online through the Chevening application system during the open round
Apply to three different eligible UK courses and secure an unconditional offer
official.application_route: Apply online during the round via chevening.org and, separately, secure offers from three eligible UK courses - the Chevening application and university applications are separate tracks.
official.study_mode: Full-time one-year master's degree in the UK
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship or legal residence in a Chevening eligible country or territory
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is for citizens or legal residents of eligible countries and territories to study in the UK
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: You may apply for any eligible UK master's course offered at a participating university
official.duration: One-year master's degree, studies beginning September or October 2027
official.description: Chevening Scholarships are fully-funded one-year master's degrees in the UK for future leaders from eligible countries and territories, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and partner organisations.
official.region: UK (award for applicants from eligible countries/territories worldwide)
official.program_type: Fully-funded master's scholarship (Chevening Awards, FCDO funded)

applicant_utility.summary: Chevening is a leadership award more than an academic grant: the published eligibility bar is two years of work experience (2,800 hours) after your undergraduate degree, a degree finished at least two years before the deadline, and a commitment to return home for two years after the award. The 2027-2028 round closed in October 2026, so the next realistic cycle opens around August 2027 for studies from September/October 2028. Applications are sifted in October, reading committees assess from mid-October to January, interviews run March-April and results land in mid-June - a ten-month process you must plan master's applications around.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professionals with 3-7 years' work experience, a clear leadership track and an argument for why a specific UK master's fits a home-country impact plan.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your work hours against the 2,800-hour rule and check your degree was completed at least two years before the deadline
Shortlist three eligible UK courses at participating universities before the round opens; one unconditional offer must follow
Prepare to upload documents at least seven working days before the interview
Draft the impact argument around return-home contribution, which the two-years condition makes binding
common_rejection_risks: Missing the two-year post-degree requirement or under-counting hours of work experience
Leaving the university applications late: the unconditional offer from one of your three courses is a condition of the award
Applying without a credible two-year-return-home plan, which the eligibility page states as a condition of the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Graduation-related costs, including flights to and from the UK for the ceremony, are explicitly not covered; no monetary award figures are published on the official pages checked.
document_audit: Interview-stage documents are due at least seven working days before your interview - late uploads risk being asked to reschedule
alerts: Applications close in October at 11:00 UTC, which is mid-afternoon in Bangladesh - do not leave it to the last day
The whole selection runs October to mid-June, so start university applications and scholarship drafts in parallel
If you return to the UK after your award for any reason, that return travel is at your own expense
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to Chevening online in the open round (August-October), apply separately to three eligible UK courses, get sifted and assessed by reading committees, attend the March-April interview, and hold the unconditional offer by the July deadline for studies from September/October.
